SUPPORT
Bennett's main utility as a Support comes from the huge flat ATK buff his Elemental Burst provides. This buff only scales with his Base Attack, so it is unaffected by any external ATK Buff.

Regarding Weapon Choices:
Mistsplitter Reforged, Azurelight and Absolution: While providing the same base ATK as Aquila Favonia, These weapons are a better choice when building for Bennett's personal damage .
Freedom-Sworn: In teams where Bennett can reliably trigger this weapon's passive, it can be stronger than Aquila Favonia, Mistsplitter Reforged and Absolution.
Peak Patrol Song: While requiring two additional normal attacks, this weapon can provide a sizeable buff with just one or two DEF% Main Stats, making it competitive with Aquila Favonia and similar options for teams that highly value DMG% buffs.
Favonius Sword: This weapon's low base attack heavily impairs Bennett's buffing potency, but it can be a viable pick in teams with extremely high Energy recharge requirements or no actual use for the attack buff.

Regarding Artifact Sets:
Instructor (4): In teams that value Elemental Mastery more than ATK%, this set pulls ahead of other options if Bennett can reliably trigger a reaction.
Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City (4): This set requires Bennett to trigger a reaction including the Element you want to be buffed. When Noblesse is already covered on the team, or the team values DMG Bonus more than Attack or Elemental Mastery, this set is a good pick.
Deepwood Memories (4): The best pick for any Dendro Damage related teams Bennett might be in. Use this if there is no other viable holder available.

DPS
Regarding Weapon Choices:
Haran Geppaku Futsu, Light of Foliar Incision, The Black Sword: When Bennett is not able to use infused Normal Attacks, these weapons perform significantly worse.
Freedom-Sworn, The Alley Flash: If Bennett is not able to trigger Melt or Vaporize frequently, these weapons perform poorly.
Summit Shaper: Assumes no shield. With a shield, this weapon performs better than similar ranking weapons.
Wolf-Fang: At [R5], this weapon performs significantly better, matching Summit Shaper.
Finale of the Deep: If you can reliably clear the Bond of Life, this weapon performs similar to Summit Shaper.

Regarding Artifact Sets:
Crimson Witch of Flames (4): This set is the best generalist pick for Bennett, as it performs great when triggering Vaporize or Melt, and still good when not triggering reactions.
Thundering Fury (4): In teams where Bennett frequently triggers electro related reactions, such as overload, this set can perform on par with Crimson Witch of Flames (4).
Marechaussee Hunter (4): When paired with Furina, this is Bennett's best set.

This section focuses on using Thoma as a trigger for Burgeon. Thoma's slow rate of Pyro application paired with frequent Fiery Collapse triggers make him a great option for Burgeon. Additionally, he provides defensive utility in the form of shields. 

Regarding Weapon Choices:
Kitain Cross Spear: High refinement is recommended to further reduce Thoma's Energy Recharge requirements
Dragon's Bane: Becomes a more reasonable option when you have Thoma's [C4].
Favonius Lance: If using this weapon, try to build some Crit Rate so Thoma can trigger the passive. 
Rightful Reward: In teams where you are able to heal Thoma consistently (overhealing also counts), Rightful Reward can be a reasonable option due to the amount of energy generation. 

Regarding Artifact Main Stats:
While building as much Elemental Mastery (with enough Energy Recharge) as possible is optimal for damage, you may use some HP% Main Stats if you desire a stronger shield. This can be relevant if running teams without other forms of defensive utility outside of Thoma's shields, and it's worth keeping in mind that Burgeon deals self-damage. 

Regarding Talent Priority: 
Thoma's talent levels do not contribute towards his Burgeon damage, so leveling them is optional in this respect. However, you may still wish to level them for stronger shielding. 

SUPPORT
This build focuses on maximising Thoma's potential as a SHIELD SUPPORT. 

Regarding Weapon Choices:
Favonius Lance: This is generally Thoma's best weapon for a SHIELD SUPPORT build, make sure to build some Crit Rate if using it so that you can trigger the passive. 
Rightful Reward: In teams where you would typically use Thoma as a SHIELD SUPPORT, it is difficult or even unfeasible to trigger this weapon passive. If you are able to trigger the passive consistently then it becomes a good option due to the HP% stat along with energy generation. 

Regarding Artifact sets:
Instructor (4): This set ideally works best in heavily reaction focused teams like Hu Tao Vape where the Elemental Mastery is utilized well. But this comes at the cost of making Thoma even more difficult to build, since you have fewer potential substat rolls using 4 star artifacts, and therefore less of a chance of hitting his Energy Recharge and HP goals.

Klee has access to a number of animation cancels that allow her to deal damage with her talents faster than normal. 

Her A1 grants her "Explosive Spark" stacks when she does a Normal Attack, Skill or Burst that when consumed, give her Charged Attacks extra DMG% and not consume Stamina.

Hexerei effects give her up to 150% DMG to her Enhanced Charged Attacks - this effect should always be active at max stacks.

Mavuika uses Fighting Spirit instead of Energy, thus any Energy Recharge substats become deadweight on her.

She gains Fighting Spirit via a Natlan character consuming Nightsoul Points, OR, the Active Character dealing damage with Normal Attacks.

Mavuika only needs half of her Burst gauge to use her Elemental Burst, however, her Burst will deal more damage the more Fighting Spirit she has accumulated.

A relatively easy, but still performing well onfield combo for melt is generally 3CA > Final slash> dash >3CA > Final slash - but this can be harder  to pull off without practice, so you can settle for 4 CA > jump > 3CA > Final slash

Her optimal onfield combo for vaporize/ kaeya melt/reactionless (monopyro/overload) is 5[2 CA > dash]- For excessive/permanent cryo/hydro aura on the enemy 6[ CA > Dash > NA  ] tend to perform better. This is also great for shield breaking

column3:
DPS
On-Field Mavuika focuses on dealing large amounts of Pyro damage while riding her motorcycle: Flamestrider. She's best played in a team with Cryo characters where she can reliably get up close with Flamestrider and trigger Melt, or she can trigger Vaporize specifically with Furina, Yelan or Mona. Mavuika relies on a character exclusive mechanic known as Fighting Spirit. See the ability tips section for more info. Due to these specific mechanics, Mavuika is also best paired with another Natlan character, with the ideal options being Citlali and Xilonen.

Regarding Weapon Choices: Rankings assume Mavuika is used with Bennett.
Beacon of the Reed Sea: Ranking assumes Mavuika does not take damage.
Verdict: Ranking assumes 1 stack.
The Unforged: Ranking assumes dynamic stacks, shielded.
Serpent Spine: this weapon assumes 3 stacks. At [R5], this weapon will perform close to Beacon of the Reed Sea in Melt teams, and close to Verdict in Vaporize teams.  At max stacks at [R5], it performs better than Redhorn Stonethresher.  It should be noted that since Mavuika inherently has many sources of Crit Rate buffs, it is easy to overcap with Serpent Spine.
Rainslasher: Weapon perform as well as Serpent Spine [R1] in a Vaporize team.
Tidal Shadow: Ranking assumes Mavuika get healing                                         

Detailed weapon calculations here:  Melt | Vaporize 

Special thanks to lego102lego for helping with the calculations!

Regarding Artifact Sets:
Marechaussee Hunter (4): Only to be used when paired with Furina - Performs mildly worse than Obsidian Codex (4).
Scroll of the Hero of Cinder City (4): If no other member of the team can hold it, this becomes Mavuika's best artifact set for Off-Field.
Deepwood Memories (4): This set is a support option in teams with a relevant amount of Dendro damage (i.e. Kinich)

Regarding Artifact Stats:
In almost all situations Mavuika will prefer an Elemental Mastery Sands over an ATK% Sands, unless she is not used in Amplifying Reaction focused team (Vaporize/Melt). It should also be noted that with many external Elemental Mastery buffs, such as Instructor (4) artifact set or Sucrose, Elemental Mastery slightly loses value.

SUPPORT
Mavuika can also take a more supportive role where she uses less field time and instead helps other DPS with her off-field damage and Pyro application, plus A4 passive giving the onfield unit a potent dmg% buff. Due to her passives, she would still like to burst in teams where she can reliably gain a large amount of Fighting Spirit both for her damage and buffing capability.

SHIELD & BUFF SUPPORT
Nicole is a potent Support that provides both a shield and a sizeable flat ATK buff to the entire team. The party member on field also gets an additional ATK buff after 3 seconds or instantly if they are a Hex character.

Regarding Weapon Choices:
Memory of Dust: As Nicole snapshots her own Attack when pressing skill, it is advised to attack a few times before using skill to benefit from this weapon's passive.
Starcaller's Watch: While not contributing a lot to high Attack, this weapon provides a reliable Damage Bonus to your onfielder.
Hakushin Ring: In teams where this weapon's passive becomes applicable, it increases in value and appreciates refinements.
Favonius Codex: This weapon can have significantly more value if the teams Energy requirements are dire.
Thrilling Tales of Dragon Slayers: This weapon severely reduces the potency of Nicole's buff, but brings a hefty buff of its own to the onfielder. Depending on the team, this weapon can be one of Nicole's best choices.
